passages.text: I have gone astray like a lost sheep. Seek your servant, for I don’t forget your commandments.
passages.note: feeling lost, wanting to be found

passages.text: My soul has had her dwelling too long with him who hates peace. I am for peace, but when I speak, they are for war.
passages.note: weary of conflict with hostile people

passages.text: I will lift up my eyes to the hills. Where does my help come from? My help comes from Yahweh, who made heaven and earth. He will not allow your foot to be moved. He who keeps you will not slumber. Behold, he who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
passages.note: seeking help and protection in hard times

passages.text: Have mercy on us, Yahweh, have mercy on us, for we have endured much contempt. Our soul is exceedingly filled with the scoffing of those who are at ease, with the contempt of the proud.
passages.note: worn down by mockery and contempt

passages.text: Our soul has escaped like a bird out of the fowler’s snare. The snare is broken, and we have escaped.
Those who sow in tears will reap in joy. He who goes out weeping, carrying seed for sowing, will certainly come again with joy, carrying his sheaves.
passages.note: hope that sorrow and effort bear fruit

passages.text: Unless Yahweh builds the house, they labor in vain who build it. Unless Yahweh watches over the city, the watchman guards it in vain. It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil; for he gives sleep to his loved ones.
passages.note: overwork, anxious striving, need for rest

passages.text: If you, Yah, kept a record of sins, Lord, who could stand? But there is forgiveness with you, therefore you are feared. I wait for Yahweh. My soul waits. I hope in his word. My soul longs for the Lord more than watchmen long for the morning; more than watchmen for the morning.

Yahweh, my heart isn’t haughty, nor my eyes lofty; nor do I concern myself with great matters, or things too wonderful for me. Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with his mother, like a weaned child is my soul within me.
passages.note: humility and quieting an anxious mind

passages.text: See how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to live together in unity!

By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down. Yes, we wept, when we remembered Zion. On the willows in that land, we hung up our harps. For there, those who led us captive asked us for songs. Those who tormented us demanded songs of joy: “Sing us one of the songs of Zion!” How can we sing Yahweh’s song in a foreign land?
passages.note: exile, homesickness, grief far from home
